messages.subject: Re: Can ggtree visualize a BEAST1.8 summary MCC tree? If so, why some NA returned in feature variables.
parts:
if you follow the guide, https://guangchuangyu.github.io/2016/07/how-to-bug-author/ (the link presented in this group), you will find that your ggtree version is out-dated.

another issue is that you need to make a good reproducible example. Don't copy paste source code that hard to follow. Don't mix source code that are irrelevant to the exact issue.



On Wed, Feb 28, 2018 at 1:49 PM, <wjn...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear Guangchuang and all ggtree experts,



I'm asking if the ggtree can visualize a summary and annotated Maximum clade credibility (MCC) tree (a .tre file including one tree) generated by BEAST 1.8 and based on a Bayesian discrete phylogeographic model to reconstruct a global migration pattern of a plant pathogen. The tree includes the sampling country/location information, but no sampling time available.


First, I plan to visualize this MCC tree using 24 customized colors for 24 different sampling locations.


However, I met one problem when I use the fortify () function in ggtree_1.6.11 to convert my tree data to a data frame, the some location names cannot be converted properly (NA), and one location name "Ivory Coast" was lost when I check the the levels of Locations as a factor in R, and the downstreaming branch color work was failed.


My detailed operation and R command line are as following for your reproducible test for my question:


(1) a summary and annotated MCC.tre file (including one tree) was saved and exported from the software TreeAnnotator in BEAST 1.8 package;


(2) however, I notice that the ggtree package and online tutorial said it can input the .tree file generated from BEAST 2.0 via read.beast() function, and after my attempt,  it doesn't work for the .tree file generated by BEAST 1.8. So, I open my generated MCC.tre file using FigTree 1.4.3, and color the branch by locations using its default color scheme, and then save the resulting figure and exported the tree file as a .nexus file and checked the box "Include Annotations (NEXUS & JSON only)".


My first question is can I import my BEAST 1.8 MCC tree into R using ggtree like what I did above, or any other better way/function that I can do it?


(3) Then I read this exported MCCtree.nexus file into R using ggtree function read.beast()


library("ggtree")


# Import the .nexus file of MCC tree

mcctree <-  read.beast("figtreetest.nexus")


# Check the mcctree object


mcctree

'beast' S4 object that stored information of

'figtreetest.nexus'.


...@ tree:

Phylogenetic tree with 84 tips and 83 internal nodes.


Tip labels:

P8705_Cox2_Philippines, P8716_Cox2_Philippines, P8690_Cox2_Philippines, P7545_Cox2_Philippines, P7537_Cox2_Philippines, P11007_Cox2_Guam, ...


Rooted; includes branch lengths.


with the following features available:

'Cox2_for_BEAUTi.rate', 'height', 'height_0.95_HPD', 'height_median', 'height_range',

'length', 'length_0.95_HPD', 'length_median', 'length_range', 'Locations',

'Locations.prob', 'Locations.rate', 'Locations.set', 'Locations.set.prob', 'posterior',

.


# Convert the "mcctree" above to a data frame for the downstreaming customized branch color.


mcctree_data <- fortify(mcctree)


write.csv(mcctree_data, file="mcctree_data.csv")


However, I found some attached feature variables (i.e. height, locations, etc) of the tips of some locations including Sri Lanka, Ivory Coast, Hawaii USA, Costa Rica, Florida USA, French Polynesia,Ivory Coast and Papua New Guinea was lost and returned "NA" in the R data frame. Please note that all the "space" between the single words within one country name was removed automatically in the .csv file, when I save this data frame as a .csv file. Please review this problem in the attached "mcctree_data.csv" file.

In addition, the location "Ivory Coast" was lost from the total 24 locations in my analyses, when I check the locations names as following.


levels(as.factor(as.character(mcctree_data$Locations)))

[22] "Venezuela"        "Zaire"


Thus, due to the "NA" error and "Ivory Coast" lost, I cannot find out a correct data file including the "node" number and corresponding "Locations" for the merge and final color mapping on all the branches of the tree.




I will be appreciated a lot if you'd like provide a solution to resolve my problem when I convert my tree file to a data.frame for the downstreaming analyses, although after I replaced the NAs with the correct location information, I used the commands below to visualize my tree.


# Extract the "node", "label", "Locations" columns only for a new data frame.

In addition, I tried to use the tidy function from the tidytree package in R 3.4.of our High Performance Cluster and attempted to convert my mcc tree object to a dataframe, however, the returned messages said this function cannot convert a beast class 4 object.



Summary of my questions:


Can ggtree or even treeio packages customize all branches colors of a MCC tree from BEAST1.8 using the associated feature variable "Location"? Specifically:


(1) Is there a way or function for ggtree to read a BEAST 1.8 summary and annotated MCC tree with feature variables into R and edit by ggtree? Is my operation described above a correct way to do this? Or are there other solutions you'd like to advice available?


(2) How can I convert the MCC tree object to correct data frame without these "NA"s? Are there any functions or solutions available?


I attached all the files that I mentioned above for your reproducible test.


The attached are (1) my original summary and annotated MCC.tre file produced from TreeAnnotator, (2) my exported .nexus file of the MCC tree including all the annotation information, (3) the converted tree data frame as a .csv file and including some "NA"s, and (4) the customized color MCC tree that I obtained using ggtree, when I replaced the correct "Locations" names manually.



Any solutions will be appreciated.

Thank you very much for your time and concern!


Best,

Jianan Wang
